Browse Blooio number inventory available to purchase. `type=shared` returns available shared lines; `type=dedicated` returns unassigned dedicated inventory. When one or more `area_code` values are supplied with `type=dedicated` or `type=inbound`, the response is an area-code quote: each requested code is reported as either in stock (provisioned free) or requiring a custom order (a custom area-code fee applies and a provisioning ticket is opened at purchase). operations.name: purchase_blooio_numbers
operations.description:
Purchase Blooio numbers

Purchase one or more Blooio lines. Purchases are asynchronous and billable: the call charges the organization's credit balance, then its default payment method, and returns a `purchase_id`; the lines are provisioned when Stripe confirms the invoice, at which point a `number.purchase.completed` webhook fires (or `number.purchase.failed`). A card requiring 3DS/SCA returns `status: action_required` with an `action_url`, and also emits `number.purchase.action_required`.

quantity.description: Number of new lines (dedicated/inbound). Shared is always 1.

area_codes.description: Preferred 3-digit US area codes (dedicated/inbound). Out-of-stock codes incur a custom fee and open a ticket.

zip_codes.description: Preferred ZIP codes (dedicated/inbound), used when an area code is not specified.

Get channel settings

Per-channel settings for channel types that support them. `settings` and `available` are per channel type: Blooio (P2P numbers) exposes `auto_mark_read`, `auto_share_contact`, and `imessage_only`; Apple Messages for Business and WhatsApp Business expose `opener`; Blooio Voice exposes `inbound`, who answers the number's calls and how long they ring. `available[key]` says whether THIS channel may turn `key` on (type-gated). A channel whose type has no settings yet returns `403 settings_unsupported_for_channel_type`.

operations.name: update_channel_settings
operations.description:
Update channel settings

Partial update of a channel's settings (send only the keys you want to change). Keys are per channel type. Blooio (P2P numbers): `auto_mark_read` is available on dedicated and inbound lines; `auto_share_contact` is dedicated-only AND the line must have a contact card (name or photo) set up; `imessage_only` is available on every line. Apple Messages for Business and WhatsApp Business: `opener`, a partial update of the channel's opener (send only the fields you want to change). Blooio Voice: `inbound`, with `handler` (`softphone` or `agent`) and `ring_timeout_seconds` (5 to 120); `agent` needs a live Blooio agent that owns the number. Turning a setting OFF is always allowed. Errors return a machine-readable `code`: `settings_unsupported_for_channel_type` (403, a channel type without settings), `auto_mark_read_not_allowed` / `auto_share_contact_not_allowed` (403, line type can't enable it), `contact_card_not_set_up` (403, enable auto_share_contact with no contact card), `agent_unavailable` (409, the `agent` handler on a number no live Blooio agent owns), `no_settings_provided` (422, empty update), `invalid_settings` (422, unknown key or field, a value of the wrong type, or an opener…

auto_share_contact.description: Blooio: share the number's Name & Photo card with people who message it. Dedicated lines only, and the line must have a contact card set up.

Ask for a rejected campaign (`review_failed` or `mno_rejected`) to be reviewed again, saying what you fixed. An appeal charges a review fee, refunded if the registry rejects the request. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

operations.name: get_rcs_brand
operations.description:
Get the RCS brand

The organization's RCS brand. While it's `in_review`, reading it checks the review for news. OAuth apps need `numbers:read`.

operations.name: put_rcs_brand
operations.description:
Register the RCS brand

Register the organization's RCS brand and send it for review, or resubmit a `rejected` or `failed` one with corrected details. Once it's submitted the brand can't change, except its point of contact through `POST /rcs/brand/changes`. `registration.rcs_brand.updated` fires as its `status` changes. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

display_name.description: The brand's name as people know it.

ein.description: US Employer Identification Number: nine digits, optionally `NN-NNNNNNN`.

operations.name: request_rcs_brand_change
operations.description:
Request a change to the RCS brand's contact

Pay to change the point of contact of a brand that's `in_review` or `verified`; send only the fields that change. The request is charged once, whatever it changes, and Blooio carries it to Google. The brand keeps its contact until the request is `applied`. The brand has one open request at a time. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

List RCS senders

The organization's RCS senders, newest first. OAuth apps need `numbers:read`.

operations.name: create_rcs_sender
operations.description:
Create an RCS sender

Draft a sender under the organization's brand. It's an `rcs_business` channel from the start, `pending_verification` until Google verifies it, and nothing is sent for review until `POST /rcs/senders/{channelId}/submit`. Upload the logo and banner with `POST /rcs/assets` first. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

use_case.description: What the sender mostly sends. Carriers review its launch against it.

profile.description: What people see on the sender in Google Messages. Creating a sender needs every field but the contacts, and at least one of `phone`, `email`, and `website`.

operations.name: get_rcs_sender
operations.description:
Get an RCS sender

One of the organization's RCS senders. While it's under review, reading it checks the review for news. OAuth apps need `numbers:read`.

operations.name: update_rcs_sender
operations.description:
Update a draft RCS sender

Change a `draft` sender's use case or profile fields; fields you leave out keep their values. Set `phone`, `email`, or `website` to `null` to remove it; one must remain. A submitted sender's name, logo, and banner change through `POST /rcs/senders/{channelId}/changes`. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

use_case.description: What the sender mostly sends. Carriers review its launch against it.

profile.description: What people see on the sender in Google Messages. Creating a sender needs every field but the contacts, and at least one of `phone`, `email`, and `website`.

brand_color.description: Hex color for the sender's buttons and accents.

operations.name: remove_rcs_sender
operations.description:
Remove an RCS sender

Stop using a sender for good: its channel stops sending and receiving, and its monthly fee stops, with the rest of the period credited. A sender Google has is then deleted there, which shows in `GET /rcs/changes` as a `sender_removal` request. Fees already charged aren't refunded. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

operations.name: submit_rcs_sender
operations.description:
Submit an RCS sender

Send a draft sender to Google for verification. The brand must be `verified`. Submitting charges the sender's verification, renewed yearly, and starts its monthly fee; if the registry refuses the sender, its verification is refunded, its month is credited back, and it stays a draft. Once submitted, add test devices and request the carrier launch; `registration.rcs_sender.updated` fires as its `status`, `section_statuses`, or `carrier_approvals` change. A retry after a lost response finds the same submission. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

operations.name: launch_rcs_sender
operations.description:
Request an RCS sender's launch

Ask the US carriers to launch a submitted sender, so it can message anyone rather than only its test devices. Carriers review how people opt in and what they'll receive; each carrier's answer arrives in `carrier_approvals`, and the sender is `live` once they approve. The launch details can be sent once. The organization needs credit or a card on file; the one-time launch fee is billed when T-Mobile approves, from the credit first. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

message_examples.description: Messages as recipients will see them.

call_to_action.description: The words people see where they opt in.

call_to_action_url.description: Required with `WEBSITE`: where the call to action is.

call_to_action_media_url.description: Required with `WEBSITE` or `MOBILE_APP`: an `opt_in_media` screenshot from `POST /rcs/assets`.

double_opt_in_message.description: Required when `double_opt_in` is true: the message that asks people to confirm.

opt_in_message.description: The first message people get after opting in.

test_video_url.description: A `test_video` from `POST /rcs/assets`, showing the sender in use.

test_notes.description: Anything reviewers need to try the sender.

operations.name: request_rcs_sender_change
operations.description:
Request a change to an RCS sender

Pay to change a submitted sender's `display_name`, `logo_url`, or `banner_url`; send only the fields that change. Each field changed is charged when you request it, and Blooio carries the change to Google and the carriers, who review it again. The sender keeps its profile until the request is `applied`. A sender has one open request at a time. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

operations.description:

operations.name: upload_rcs_asset
operations.description:
Upload an RCS asset

Host an image or video a sender's profile or launch request points to, and get back its URL. Each `kind` has its own limits: `logo` is a 224×224 PNG or JPEG up to 50 KB; `banner` is a 1440×448 PNG or JPEG up to 200 KB; `opt_in_media` is a PNG or JPEG screenshot of the opt-in call to action, up to 5 MB; `test_video` is an MP4 or QuickTime video of the sender in use, up to 50 MB. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.

operations.description:
Cancel an RCS change request

Withdraw a change request that's still `requested`, and refund its fees. Canceling again is safe. A sender removal can't be canceled. OAuth apps need `numbers:manage`.
